To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the wellbeing of fisher communities can be improved by: 1) strengthening the relational wellbeing component of fisher wellbeing through the creation of a strong social fabric; 2) promoting conservation of marine and coastal resources; and 3) improving material wellbeing by providing access to education and employment opportunities.

the relational component of wellbeing is a key factor for resilience and recovery of fishers and their communities after environmental disasters, and that the involvement of fisher communities in conservation initiatives is a promising strategy for both environmental and wellbeing recovery.

1) a three-dimensional wellbeing framework can help us understand how environmental impacts affect wellbeing, and how fishers deal with such impacts; 2) in this particular case, strong relational wellbeing was key to the resilience of fishers and their community in the face of an environmental disaster; 3) the recovery of fisher wellbeing is closely linked to the recovery of the environment, and 4) the potential of conservation initiatives for building wellbeing and community resilience should be more fully recognized by government policy
In summary, our research is concerned with
the wellbeing and resilience of coastal communities and their ability to adapt to environmental change.
the wellbeing of a group of urban fishers and the community in which they reside, in a context of environmental impacts, disasters, and recovery.
understanding the impacts of environmental damage and disaster on wellbeing, and how fisher communities can build resilience and recover from these impacts.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the wellbeing of fisher communities is not only a function of the ecological state of their environment, but also of the relational and subjective wellbeing of the community.

the fishers of Vila dos Pesadores, and the broader community, have been able to deal well with the impacts of environmental damage and disaster because of their pre-existing strong relational wellbeing.
the wellbeing of fisher communities can be improved, in the short and long-term, by the combined actions of the government, civil society, and local communities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a holistic approach to fisher wellbeing, involving material, subjective and relational wellbeing components, is essential for effective environmental policy.

the wellbeing of fisher communities is strongly affected by a range of environmental damages and disasters, and that the resilience of fishers to these impacts can be greatly increased by the development of strong relational wellbeing and the involvement of fisher communities in conservation initiatives.

a holistic wellbeing approach, which includes material, subjective and relational wellbeing dimensions, can help to better understand and address environmental impacts on fishers, and to support the resilience of fisher communities.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, to be effective in promoting wellbeing and resilience in fishing communities, conservation initiatives should involve fishers in decision-making and implementation, and should be accompanied by policies that promote social wellbeing.
, when considering the impacts of environmental damages and disasters on fishers and fishing dependent communities, a focus on material and subjective wellbeing is not sufficient.
, in the context of urban coastal communities in developing countries, environmental disasters are not just ecological or physical events.
